name: Framer
tagline: Design-forward website builder with CMS, animations, and hosting

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Basic listed at $10/month billed yearly, with higher tiers and monthly billing options.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Framer subdomain; 1 GB bandwidth; 10 CMS collections; 1,000 pages; 5 MB file uploads; 1 free locale; up to 3 editors; 500 AI credits to try
tiers.notes: Custom domains require a paid site plan.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 30 pages; 2 CMS collections; 1,000 CMS items; 50 GB bandwidth/month; 1,000 AI credits/month; up to 10 editors
tiers.notes: Pricing page was displaying yearly billing at $10/month; the exact monthly-billed site price was not exposed in accessible page text.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 150 pages; 10 CMS collections; 2,500 CMS items; 100 GB bandwidth/month; 3,000 AI credits/month; up to 10 editors
tiers.notes: Pricing page was displaying yearly billing at $30/month; the exact monthly-billed site price was not exposed in accessible page text.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom limits; unlimited editors; enterprise security, uptime guarantee, SCIM and SSO

pricing.freeTierCaps: Framer subdomain; 1 GB bandwidth; 10 CMS collections; 1,000 pages; 5 MB upload limit; 1 locale; up to 3 editors; 500 trial AI credits
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual for Basic and Pro; annual billed upfront, while added editors and usage on annual plans are billed monthly
pricing.hiddenCosts: Extra design editors are $20/month each and content editors $10/month each; locales cost $20/month each; Pro expansion is metered ($20 per extra 100 pages, $40 per 10 CMS collections, $20 per 10,000 CMS items, $40 per 100 GB bandwidth), Convert starts at $50 per 500,000 events, and Advanced Hosting costs $200/month.

verdictSummary: You can build a simple AI/site generator and host static pages, but Framer's animation/design editor, CMS, hosting, templates, and publishing polish are real product depth.
coreLoopDIY: Generate site sections, edit them visually, save JSON/page data, and deploy static output to a host.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because polished landing pages ship quickly with minimal design-engineering friction.

priorArt.name: GrapesJS
priorArt.desc: Open-source web builder framework useful for a DIY site editor.

alternatives.name: Plasmic
alternatives.desc: A hosted visual builder with CMS, interactions, Figma import and a custom domain free; the badge remains.

rejectedAlternatives.name: GrapesJS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A framework for making visual editors, not a hosted animated site builder.

rejectedAlternatives.name: TeleportHQ
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The old free-plan advice is stale: current pricing gives a seven-day trial and then asks for an editor subscription.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Webstudio
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The open core builds excellent sites and CMS pages, but Framer-grade animation is not a complete free equivalent.

notes: Good modern website-builder target with a plausible DIY core.
prompt:
Build me a landing-page workshop to replace Framer. Requirements:

- A static site setup: Astro with Tailwind, building to plain files. No
  database, no server at runtime.
- A section library as components with props: hero, feature grid, testimonial,
  pricing table, FAQ, footer. All copy for a site lives in one content.json.
- New-site flow: I describe the product, an LLM (key in .env) drafts
  content.json, then I edit copy by hand from there. Generation is a helper
  script, not a runtime dependency.
- One theme file for fonts, colors, and spacing so every page looks consistent
  without per-page design work.
- Live preview via `astro dev`; `npm run build` emits dist/ ready to host.
- deploy.sh that rsyncs dist/ to my VPS (or any static host).
- Sites live in ./sites/<name>/ under git; no accounts, no telemetry, the only
  network call is the optional LLM draft.
- Out of scope: a visual drag-and-drop editor, scroll animations, a CMS UI,
  and forms. I edit files; the section library is the product here.
- README: setup, deploy config, and how to add a new section component.
